beats.narration: An Android app asks for your location. You're actually making two choices.
beats.visual: Phone permission prompt splits into two labelled dials: WHEN and HOW EXACT.

beats.narration: Tap yes too fast, and you can miss what you just gave away.
beats.visual: Thumb taps 'Allow'; the two dials blur past.

beats.narration: First: when. In the foreground, roughly while you're using the app, or in the background. On Android 11 and newer, the pop-up can't grant background access; that's a separate switch on a settings page. Second: how exact. Precise, or approximate. Grant approximate, and that's all the app gets, even in the background.
beats.visual: Diagram: WHEN dial (foreground / background, with a settings-page icon on background); HOW EXACT dial (precise pin vs. wide circle). Illustration.

beats.narration: So check which apps have background access, and choose approximate wherever your exact spot isn't needed.
beats.visual: Checklist card: 1) background access, 2) approximate where enough.

beats.narration: And on Android 10 and newer, the first time an app uses your location in the background, Android sends a reminder. That's your moment to decide again.
beats.visual: Notification card slides in: 'reminder: this app can use location all the time' (illustrative wording). Illustration.

caption:
When an Android app asks for your location, you're making two choices: when (foreground or background) and how exact (precise or approximate).
